final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the actor provided no new admissible evidence; the response is a narrower interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation matters at the claim-framing level: the actor is no longer fairly read as asserting clean compliance or treating stale approval and informal monitoring as full substitutes. But the policy predicate for certification still is not met on the present evidence. The governing text requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses, unless the weakness is covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance. The record still lacks both the current disclosure artifact and any approved mitigation or acceptance. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness, but they do not satisfy the certification condition for this documented subgroup regression. That is the distinction: a caveated position can be intellectually narrower than an uncaveated certification claim, yet still remain unsupported as a compliance conclusion when the caveat itself depends on missing evidence. Accordingly, the packet remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
